newsitem.title: UK: Britain worried by planned Cyprus missile purchase.
newsitem.headline: Britain worried by planned Cyprus missile purchase.

text.p: A Greek Cypriot decision to buy Russian surface-to-air missiles could destabilise what is already one of the most heavily militarised areas of the world, the British Foreign Office said on Monday.

Asked by Reuters for comment on the decision, a Foreign Office spokesman said: "The foreign secretary made it quite clear the international community has indicated further increases in military strength on either side would be of serious concern, and we would reiterate that point."
On a visit to the divided island last month, Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind told Greek Cypriot leaders the planned purchase would be a "big step in the wrong direction."

The planned acquisition of the S-300 system would neutralise the air superiority Turkey has had since 1974, when its troops invaded the northern third of Cyprus in response to a short-lived coup engineered by the military then ruling Greece.
Tension has increased perceptibly on the island in the past six months after the deaths of four people in ceasefire line incidents and both sides continue to build up their defences.

Rifkind described the level of militarisation on both sides as "absurdly high and dangerously high". The missile system, which has a 150 km (90 mile) range, is the first step by the Cypriot government to building a credible air defence system.

The United Nations have little to show for 20 years of attempts to broker peace and the Greek Cypriot side reacted coolly to a 10-point plan which Rifkind unveiled in a bid to set peace talks in motion.
